slot.brief: Electron in a hydrogen-like atom jumps between two given levels; find the emitted photon energy or wavelength using Bohr energy formula.

stem: In a $\text{He}^+$ ion, an electron makes a transition from $n=3$ to $n=2$. What is the wavelength of the emitted photon? Take $R = 1.097\times10^7$ m$^{-1}$.
working:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda}=RZ^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2^2}-\dfrac{1}{3^2}\right)$, with $Z=2$. 
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda}=1.097\times10^7\times4\times\dfrac{5}{36}=6.094\times10^6$ m$^{-1}$. 
$\lambda=1.641\times10^{-7}$ m $\approx 164$ nm.

Independent check: For He⁺, 1/λ = RZ²(1/2² − 1/3²) = (5/9)R, so λ ≈ 1.64 × 10⁻⁷ m = 164 nm.
solution:
For a hydrogen-like ion, $\frac{1}{\text{λ}}=RZ^2\big(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\big)$, with $Z=2$.
$$\frac{1}{\text{λ}}=1.097\times10^7\times4\times\frac{5}{36}=6.094\times10^6\text{ m}^{-1}$$
Thus, $\text{λ}=1.641\times10^{-7}\text{ m}\approx164\text{ nm}$.
